newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas drops, nearbys off but only 7 deals done.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas drops, nearbys off but only 7 deals done.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract was weaker in all but one of the traded months on Monday, with losses of up to 0.20 pence a therm seen.

But volumes were thin, with only 60 lots traded over the day in only seven separate transactions. A futures broker pointed out that Mondays are frequently slow, with many players still working out their strategies for the coming week.
The falls were seen as modest, given that prompt gas had traded on the flexibility mechanism over the weekend at down to -14.65 stg a therm, and many had expected futures losses to be greater.
"I thought April held up reasonably well," said a broker, although he added that bids had fallen away considerably.
"By the look of it, the market could go weaker in the prompt," he said, while pointing out that the back months - mostly untraded on Monday - were looking relatively strong.

There were far more offers on the market than bids, across all periods but particularly the front months. At one point the best bid for April was for 10 lots, while the best offer had a depth of 125 lots.
April was last traded at 9.70 pence, down by 0.125 pence from Friday's settlement, May was down 0.055 to 9.90 pence, and June was off by 0.20 pence a therm to 9.80 pence at the last trade.
Only October was firmer, trading at 12.275, up by 0.20 pence from Friday. A total of 25 lots were traded in the morning and 35 in the afternoon.
